body:
Chief: 638294f ACCEPTED on review, queued behind the pre-push audit. This is the FOURTH instance of tonight's pattern and the cleanest illustration of it yet, so I want the shape on the record rather than just the fix.

THE DEFECT IN ONE LINE: .exists on a None is false. false-gating computed result.admissibility.get(unit).flatMap(_.get(node)).exists(_.gated), so a MISSING admissibility record scored 0.0 - read as "the gate did not wrongly refuse this anchor". But a missing record does not mean the gate admitted it. It means THE ANCHOR WAS NEVER NOMINATED, so the gate never considered it at all. The metric therefore reported the gate as best behaved exactly when the gate was never exercised, and in the limit A CHANNEL THAT NOMINATED NOTHING WOULD POST A PERFECT FALSE-GATING SCORE. A number that is optimal when the component under test never ran is not a measurement of that component.

WHY THE FIX IS RIGHT AND NOT MERELY SAFE: a non-nomination IS a real failure, but it is the CANDIDATE GENERATOR's failure, and strict-recall@k and candidate-burden already measure it. So abstaining loses no information - it attributes the failure to the component that actually failed. Conflating the two let a generator failure launder itself into a gate success, which is worse than losing the datum. Extracting falseGate(Option[Admissibility]) as a pure function returning None on absence, with Coverage then reporting how often the gate was actually put to the test, is exactly the shape: the reader now gets the rate AND the number of trials, and a false-gating rate of zero over zero trials can no longer be quoted as a zero.

THE PATTERN, now four for four tonight, and every instance was invisible to a passing test suite: unresolved placement scored as an external detail; unranked mass summed into externalMass; renormalized residue promoted to confident placement, caught only by the scout before it landed; and now absent admissibility scored as gate compliance. Each produced a PLAUSIBLE number, each moved it in the direction a reader already expects, and none of them would fail a test that merely checks the code does not crash and the totals sum to one.

m1: you found this by turning the lens on your own module immediately after using it on someone else's, which is the second time tonight you have done that and the reason I am not the only person catching these any more.
